key_insight: Neutral ethylenediamine reconstructs tin-rich tin–lead perovskite surfaces by chelating undercoordinated metals and removing excess tin, reducing interfacial recombination.
engineering_relevance: Controlling surface stoichiometry and passivating-species chemistry can improve electron extraction into C60 and guide more efficient tin–lead perovskite solar cells.
method: Compare neutral ethylenediamine and protonated ethylenediammonium iodide surface reactions.
Use atomistic simulations to examine vacancy-assisted iodide migration and deprotonation.
Apply surface reconstruction to methylammonium-free solar cells.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports 25.86% power conversion efficiency and simulations showing that subsurface iodide vacancies lower the energetic cost of deprotonation.
watch_item: The abstract does not establish long-term operational stability or manufacturing-scale reproducibility of the surface treatment.
paper_title: Controlling Surface Chemistry in Tin-Lead Perovskites for High-Efficiency Solar Cells
